plan.etaReasoning:
Ten lanes, each scoped to 5.5-6 h of work, run concurrently: ~59.5 h of engineering compressed to a ~6 h critical path. Add ~1 h for the serialized integration window on src/legacy-main.ts (L1 receives call-site patches from L5, L7 and L4, and will trip source-text pins in the 82 test files that string-match that file), and ~1 h for final verification. Total 8 h to a fully integrated, verified HITL build.

Two things set that path, not the sum of the work.

First, src/legacy-main.ts. Four lanes need call sites in it and the repo's own discipline doc names it the file every agent serializes on. L1 owns it outright and everyone else hands it a bounded patch; L1 is therefore the critical path and cannot be parallelised away.

Second, the GPU. ~3 GB free VRAM with a local LLM server holding 13 GB means only one browser QA session at a time. L2 (bake check), L5 (WebGPU water captures), L7 (six-arena raytraced CDP sweep), L9 (three-window succession run) and L4 (chopper e2e + playtest stills) all need it. Budget one serialized window of ~60-75 min total and schedule it as lanes finish rather than at the end.

Verification cost per integration is small: full suite ~26 s, production build ~3 min, six-arena WebGPU boot ~5 min. Run the suite per lane, build and boot-check only at the integration window and once more at the end. Budget one 30-min manual smoke playtest before handing over - the owner tests by playing, and none of these lanes is proven by a green suite alone.

Intermediate checkpoint, since he is only away a few hours: at ~3.5 h the three lanes he will notice first (L1 dead controls, L2 arena scale, L4 HUD bounce) should be landable as a build he can actually play, with the rest arriving at the 8 h mark. If the choice is between an 8 h complete build and a 3.5 h partial one, take the 3.5 h checkpoint - 'the emote button works, the arena is visibly bigger, the HUD stopped bouncing' answers the 'this is the same as 2 days ago' complaint directly, and the gate and netcode lanes do not.
topRisks: The default render profile hides procedural work, and this has already burned one owner request. resolveRenderProfile returns 'blender' by default; src/blender-environment.ts:263 sets proceduralWorld.visible = false and mirrors only 3 objects across. That is why HF-383's arena scale-up is invisible to the owner today. L3's prop and cover work runs the same risk - its FIRST task is a 20-minute check of whether that art renders on Quality at all. If it does not, L3 must re-scope onto L2's bake path or the pass ships another invisible fix.

src/legacy-main.ts is a single 33,694-line serialization point that four lanes depend on. If L1 stalls or its edits trip the 82 source-text pins in ways that cascade, the entire owner-visible half of the pass stalls with it. Mitigation: L1 starts immediately, takes the emote and stance work first (the two dead controls), and accepts handoff patches only after those land.

GPU contention is the second critical path and is easy to underestimate. Five lanes need real WebGPU browser sessions on ~3 GB of free VRAM. Unserialized, they will evict each other and produce exactly the kind of flaky, unreproducible capture that the void viewpoint-regression run already demonstrates. One window, one lane at a time, and never kill the owner's local LLM server to make room.

Farcrysis cold admission measured 13.97 s against a 12 s fence, and only fits because 8.24 s of it sits inside a yielding compileAsync. L5 and L6 both add work to that arena's cold path. If either collapses cost into one fenced submission, farcrysis stops booting entirely - the HF-374 signature. Re-measure farcrysis cold admission before the HITL handover, not after.

The HF-388 arms re-export can make the arms look worse, not better.
